title: Trigonometric Proof
page_title: Trigonometric Proof | Edexcel International A Level (IAL) Maths Revision Notes 2020

blocks.text: How do I prove harder identities?

blocks.md:
- You can use trigonometric identities you already know to prove new identities
- Make sure you know the **simple trigonometric identities** and **further trigonometric identities**
- To prove an identity start on one side and proceed step by step until you get to the other side

blocks.alt: Trig Proof Illustr 1, A Level & AS Maths: Pure revision notes

blocks.md: - Clever substitution into the **compound angle formulae **can be a useful tool for proving identities

blocks.alt: Trig Proof Illustr 2, A Level & AS Level Pure Maths Revision Notes

blocks.md: - Make sure you are confident handling fractions and fractions-within-fractions

blocks.alt: Trig Proof Illustr 3, A Level & AS Maths: Pure revision notes

blocks.md: - Always keep an eye on the 'target' expression – this can help suggest what identities to use

blocks.label: Exam Hint
blocks.md:
- Don't forget that you can start a proof from either end – sometimes it might be easier to start from the right-hand side (see the Worked Example)
- A number of trigonometric identities are given to you in the formulae booklet – make sure you know which ones are (and aren't) in there
